title: Open DS scheme
description: A full design system as data: every grammar question answered with why and because, usage rules for every situation, voice and tone, scenarios, themes (brands × light and dark) and DTCG tokens in three tiers. Tools build CSS, components, docs and agent files from it.

id.description: Scheme id; also the CLI argument and the file name.

name.description: Scheme name as shown to people.

status.description: draft: the answers may still change; curated: reviewed and settled.

summary.description: One sentence: what the scheme is for.

description.description: A paragraph an agent can read cold to understand the scheme.

ai.description: Guidance for an agent choosing or applying the scheme.

use_when.description: Products and contexts this scheme fits.

avoid_when.description: Products and contexts this scheme does not fit.

example_products.description: Kinds of products that would pick this scheme.

scenarios.description: Use scenarios: real work, written from the answers to the use scenario questions (scenarios.q1, scenarios.q2) and other reasons.

voice.description: The written outputs of the voice and tone scope. Each lists the answers it follows. The tone per moment lives in usage, under the voice situations.

principles.description: Rules a writer or an agent follows.

words.description: Words to use and words to avoid.

follows.description: Question ids whose answers this text was written from.

brands.description: Per-brand tone, for multi-brand schemes. Keys are brand ids.

inventory.description: The components this system carries: an output of the components answers, picked from the grammar catalogue. Every catalogue item is decided (OD-211): in, with why (a limited use says where it fits), or out, with the reason argued from the answers.

follows.description: Question ids whose answers picked the inventory.

id.description: A catalogue item id from the grammar.

why.description: Why it is in or out, in one sentence.

variants.description: For every variant in the component's reference, by axis then variant id: how this design system uses it, or that it does not.

additionalProperties.description: This design system's decision on one variant: how it uses it, or that it does not. Always follows from answers (because).

use.description: What this design system uses the variant for.

not_used.description: True when this design system does not use the variant.

why.description: Why it is not used (required with not_used), or more reason for the use.

because.description: The question ids whose answers this decision follows from. Required: a decision with no answer above it is not part of the scheme.

in.description: The components in the inventory, each with why.

id.description: A catalogue item id from the grammar.

why.description: Why this design system leaves it out, in one or two short sentences, from its people and answers.

instead.description: Components in this design system's inventory to use instead.

because.description: The answers (question ids) the decision rests on.

out.description: Every catalogue item not in the in list, each with why this design system leaves it out (OD-211), and what it uses instead.

samples.description: Sample content for showing this system: written from its use scenarios, in its voice, with every status mapped to a meaning. Storybook, the site and the docs read it. Each component in the inventory needs its part; parts for components outside the inventory are not used.

follows.description: Question ids whose answers the samples are written from.

screen.description: The title of a typical screen in this product.

primary.description: The action that completes the task.

meaning.description: What the status means; it picks the badge tone.

why.description: Why the status has this meaning.

statuses.description: Status labels, each with its meaning. Danger only when something failed or will be lost.

numeric.description: True for numbers that align right.

cells.description: One value per column before the status.

invalid.description: A value that triggers the error.

switches.description: Switch labels: settings that apply at once.

confirm.description: A confirm dialog for an action that is hard to undo.

destroys.description: True when confirming destroys data, so the confirm is Button danger. False when it can be undone, so the confirm is Button primary (OD-222).

tabs.description: Tabs, each with its panel text.

trigger.description: Accessible name of the menu button.

icon_action.description: The name of an icon-only action, shown in its tooltip.

conversation.description: A short conversation (OD-214), for the message, bubble, marker, attachment and message-scroller examples.

marker.description: A divider inside the conversation, such as a day.

author.description: Who wrote it: a role, not a person's name.

time.description: When it was sent, as people read it.

text.description: What it says, in the scheme's voice.

type.description: The file type, as people read it.

size.description: The file size, as people read it.

attachment.description: A file shared in the conversation.

themes.description: Every brand × mode pair the scheme ships. Light and dark are standard for every brand.

answers.description: One answer for every grammar question.

considers.description: For a question that lists what an answer must weigh (OD-245): how this answer meets each one, by its id.

because.description: Earlier question ids whose answers pulled this one.

usage.description: When to use what: one rule for every grammar situation.

use.description: The token, component, variant or tone to use.

because.description: Question ids whose answers this rule follows from.

example.description: Real copy that follows the rule. Voice situations always have one.

uses.description: The components (and variants) the rule's use names, as data, so tools need not read the prose.

component.description: A component id in this scheme's inventory.

axis.description: The variant axis, for example variant or size.

variant.description: A variant id on that axis.

tokens.description: DTCG tokens in four tiers. Primitives are the raw options, steps only (color by hue, mode and step: color.<hue>.light.<step>, color.<hue>.dark.<step>). Each brand's theme picks from them, per mode, and decides each concept's base (@). Semantics are the plain keys components read, on the same paths as the theme; a brand-dependent one points at {theme.<path>}, which the build resolves to the active brand and mode. Only semantic and component keys ship as CSS variables. Component keys point to semantics. content holds the voice scope's words.

primitive.description: Raw options shared by every brand: color hues (light ramp and dark ramp, steps only), space, size, radius, border width, font families, sizes, weights and line heights, shadows, durations, easing and opacity. Components never read them.

brands.description: Brands keyed by id. A single-brand scheme has one brand, 'default'. Each brand's theme picks primitives for the brand-dependent semantic keys.

theme.description: The brand's theme: the decision layer. Its tree has the same paths as the semantic keys it serves (color.action.primary.@, color.action.primary.hover), and each token picks a primitive. A concept with variants has a base, @, which each mode decides for itself. Build-time only: semantics resolve through it and it never ships as CSS variables.

neutral.description: The decision behind color.neutral (OD-228): which gray from the grammar's menu the neutral scale points at, and why.

gray.description: A gray from the grammar's semantics.neutral.grays.

temperature.description: The gray's temperature, as the menu names it.

why.description: Why this scheme picks this gray.

base.description: Mode-free picks: font families and corners.

light.description: Light mode picks: colors and shadows.

dark.description: Dark mode picks; the same keys as light.

semantic.description: The plain keys components and agents read: color, space, size, radius, type, motion, elevation. A brand- or mode-dependent key's value is {theme.<its own path>}. A concept with variants has a base, @, beside them: color.action.primary.@ and color.action.primary.hover.

component.description: The component API: one key per grammar component key.

content.description: Voice tokens: words for common actions, $type string. Not written to CSS.

group.description: A DTCG group: tokens and nested groups, with an optional $description and $type (inherited by its tokens). @ is the concept's base (default) value, beside its variants.

$type.description: Type inherited by every token in the group.

$extensions.description: Open DS decisions on a group that are not values.

open-ds.description: Open DS decisions on a group: how a hue's scales are generated, the component spacing map's rhythm, the spacing record or the control scale.

anyOf.description: On a colored hue: how its scales are generated (OD-223). Each mode has a key color, kept exact at 600, and optional recorded adjustments per step.

generated.description: The ticket that set the method.

light.description: The light scale's key and adjustments.

dark.description: The dark scale's key and adjustments.

@.description: The concept's base value, beside its variants, for example color.action.primary.@ next to color.action.primary.hover. The build drops the @ from the name: it becomes --color-action-primary. A reference names it: {color.action.primary.@}. Not used on primitives, which are steps only.

^[a-z0-9_-]+$.description: A token or a nested group.

scaleSpec.description: One mode's scale of a hue: its key color and any adjustments.

key.description: The key color, exact at step 600.

adjust.description: Recorded moves per step: L in OKLCH lightness, C in chroma, H in degrees, and why.

H.description: The move in hue, in degrees.

C.description: The move in OKLCH chroma: more or less color, kept inside sRGB.

token.description: A DTCG token. $value is a literal or a {path.to.token} reference.

$value.description: The value, or a reference such as {color.blue.light.600} or {theme.color-action-primary}.

$deprecated.description: DTCG: this token is kept as an alias for one minor release. Says what to use instead.

$extensions.description: Open DS decisions on a token that are not values.

open-ds.description: On a fill in a theme: its tone, which decides the text on it (OD-222, OD-227). On a component key: the fill it sits on, so the build picks its text by that fill's tone (OD-223).

why.description: On a theme pick: why this step carries the semantic's rule in this brand and mode (OD-241, OD-243).

generated.description: The why was computed by scripts/theme-reasons.mjs from the values the pick meets. Run it again after the pick changes; a why written by hand has no flag and is kept.

because.description: On a theme pick: the answers the step follows from.

tone.description: Light: the text on it is color.text.on-light. Dark: color.text.on-dark.

on.description: On a component key: the fill it sits on. The build turns a -on-light or -on-dark value into the one that fill's tone picks in each mode.

waits.description: A known shortfall on this fill, with the ticket that fixes it. The harness reports it.

multiplier.description: On a step of the component spacing map: its multiplier of space.unit.

fixed.description: On a step of the component spacing map: it holds still in this scheme.

output.description: Written text that is an output of answers, never an input.

follows.description: Question ids whose answers this text was written from.

spacingMapSpec.description: On the component spacing map (OD-235): the scheme's rhythm and the steps that hold still. The steps' values are generated from it.

rhythm.description: How much the steps grow in this scheme: a step is space.unit × its multiplier × the rhythm.

fixed.description: Steps that hold still at space.unit × their multiplier.

because.description: The answers the rhythm comes from.

spacingUseCaseSpec.description: On the space group (OD-294): the spacing record. Each space token has a use case and a multiple; its value is base × multiple.

base.description: The base step in px. The spacing.definition answer sets it: small steps on a 4px grid take 4, big even steps take 8.

use-cases.description: Each space token's use case and multiple, by its path under space, for example gap.tight.

follows.description: The answers the record is written from. It is an output of those answers, so it gives no reason to the space tokens: each token keeps its own.

why.description: The reason for the base and the multiples, in plain words.

spacingUseCase.description: One space token's use case, in the words of the grammar's spacing use_cases, and its multiple of the base.

level.description: Component: inside one component. Layout: between components.

relation.description: Inner: between parts of one thing. Container: the padding of a box around things.

reach.description: Inline: along one line. Section: between blocks. Left out when the space works both along a line and between blocks.

multiple.description: How many base steps the space is: whole or a half.

controlScaleSpec.description: On the size group (OD-294): the control scale. A control height is default + step × its step; the row is the default plus its px. size.icon is not on it.

default.description: The default control height in px. The accessibility.values answer (the target size) sets it.

step.description: The px between two steps on the control scale.

steps.description: The step of compact and large on the control scale. Default is step 0.

compact.description: Below default: a negative whole step.

large.description: At or above default. 0 when the scheme has no hero action, so large equals default.

row.description: How the table row relates to the control scale: one default control tall, plus some px.

plus.description: The px the row adds to the default control height. 0 when the scheme has no row role: the row takes the default.

follows.description: The answers the scale is written from. It is an output of those answers, so it gives no reason to the size tokens: each token keeps its own.

why.description: The reason for the default, the step and the row, in plain words.
